stem: You have an `aws_instance` whose AMI ID must change. Terraform's plan shows this forces replacement. You have `create_before_destroy = true` in its lifecycle block. What does Terraform do?
options: Terraform returns an error and refuses to proceed because the instance must be replaced.
Terraform destroys the original instance first, then creates the new one.
Terraform creates the new instance first, then destroys the original once the new one is ready.
Terraform updates the AMI ID in-place without replacing the instance.
objective: Predict the effect of create_before_destroy and ignore_changes lifecycle arguments on a planned replacement

stem: An auto-scaling group sometimes changes `desired_capacity` at runtime. Every time a teammate runs `terraform apply`, Terraform resets `desired_capacity` back to the value in the config. Which lifecycle directive stops this?
objective: Predict the effect of create_before_destroy and ignore_changes lifecycle arguments on a planned replacement

stem: A colleague adds `ignore_changes = [ami]` to an EC2 instance's lifecycle block. The AMI ID in the config is later updated to a new value. What happens on the next `terraform plan`?
options: Terraform shows an in-place update of the ami attribute.
Terraform shows a replacement because the AMI ID changed.
Terraform shows no change for the instance because the ami attribute is ignored.
Terraform returns an error because ami cannot appear in ignore_changes.
objective: Predict the effect of create_before_destroy and ignore_changes lifecycle arguments on a planned replacement
